chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Asbaat ibn Salim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him): 'We buy the 'Adl' (a bundle containing one hundred garments, a mix of good and bad), and a man comes to us and takes ninety garments from the bundle, with a profit of one dirham per dirham [of cost]. Is it befitting for us to sell the remainder based on what we sold [for the ninety]? He (peace be upon him) said: 'No, unless he buys the garment alone [separately].'

key_terms.الْعِدْل: A bundle or lot containing mixed items (here, one hundred garments)
key_terms.بِرِبْحِ دِرْهَمٍ دِرْهَمٍ: With a profit of one dirham per dirham (cost)
key_terms.دَسْتْشُمَارَ: A Persian loanword meaning a count of one hundred

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling the remainder of a mixed bundle after a portion has been sold?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the principle of *gharar* (uncertainty) in mixed-quality bulk sales, where the Imam (AS) prohibits applying a uniform profit margin to the remainder after a partial sale. Scholarly commentary highlights that this prevents hidden defects or quality disparities in the unsold portion from causing injustice, ensuring that each unit's value is determined by its actual condition rather than an arbitrary average. It underscores the Shia emphasis on transparency and fairness in commercial transactions to avoid exploitative practices.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ali Bin Asbaat Bin Salim who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We buy the bag in which are one hundred clothes, good and bad mixed (Persian), so the man comes to us and takes ninety clothes from a bad with a profit of one Dirham, one Dirham. So is it befitting for us that we sell the remainder upon similar to what we sold?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, except if he alone buys the clothes’.
en.sarwar: 8. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ali ibn Asbat from Asbat ibn Salim who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case in which we buy a bundle of a hundred or so cloths in which there are good and bad ones ‘dast shumar ’ (farsi word for mixed). A man comes and takes ninety for the bundle with profit of one dirham for each. Is it proper for us to sell the rest as just we sold?
He (the Imam) said, ‘No, unless he alone buys the cloth.’”
